nova-programme.title: Nova Programme
nova-programme.body_text:
Summary
Replace a manual, repetitive Long Term Storage (LTS) release process with an automated, deterministic pipeline across 27 Vantage components.

  Details

 Client area:  Acme Health, HC PCS MS Technology, Vantage Platform
 Our firm:  Northwind
 Duration:  12 weeks, fixed scope (charter v1.0, April 2026)
 Effort:  124 days across 5 phases

  One line purpose
Replace a manual, repetitive Long Term Storage (LTS) release process with an automated, deterministic pipeline.

  Why it exists
The manual LTS process needed many fix and retry iterations per service and stretched LTS releases to 2 3 months. Goal: predictable, traceable releases with far less manual effort.

  Approach in plain words
Two phases chained together:
1. Promote dependencies based on a software bill of materials (SBOM).
2. Run an LTS verification build per component, parse failures, auto fix known failure types, stop safely (circuit breaker) when retries run out.

Fully deterministic. No AI/ML by design.

  Scale
27 Vantage components in scope.

  Phases and milestones
  Phase                                 Weeks   Focus                                                         
             
  1 Foundation and requirements         1 3     Requirements, design, process analysis                        
  2 LTS orchestrator pipeline           4 8     Pipeline build, SBOM, promotion, verification builds          
  3 Deterministic failure remediation   9 10    Log parsing, classification, auto promotion, circuit breaker  
  4 Integration and testing             11 12   E2E tests, all 27 components, dashboards                      
  5 Deployment and rollout              12      Rollout, docs, knowledge transfer, closure                    

Milestones M1 (wk 3) foundation, M2 (wk 8) pipeline ready, M3 and M4 (wk 10) remediation and pilot, M5 (wk 11) production ready, M6 (wk 12) full deployment and handover.

  Success targets
  90% less manual dependency resolution
  80% of failures auto remediated
  85%+ accuracy in automated artifact resolution
  End state: Acme Health team runs pipeline independently

  Out of scope (headline)
Artifact repository administration, microservice code changes beyond pipeline compatibility, AI/ML, replacing existing tooling.

  Where the real detail lives
Not copied here on purpose. Open the program charter and the solution design below.

  Ion Charter
  Everest Design

  Sign off order
Northwind delivers, then Taylor Marsh (end user) signs off, then sponsor Shay Chandler gives final approval.

  People
  Project sponsor: Shay Chandler
  Primary user: Taylor Marsh, in the Beacon Systems Navigators
  Client users: Beacon Systems Navigators (users, including the primary user)
  Product Manager, manages the microservice teams: Lane Underwood
  Client owners of Vantage dsl lib and DevOps: Beacon Systems Rangers
  Our team: Northwind Sentinels


  Architecture: LTS release pipeline

  What it is
An automated, deterministic pipeline that replaces the manual Long Term Storage (LTS) release process for 27 Vantage components. No AI/ML by design.

  Context diagram
 mermaid
flowchart LR
  SBOM[SBOM per component]   P[Dependency promotion]
  P   V[LTS verification build]
  V  pass  R[Release ready]
  V  fail  L[Log parsing and classification]
  L  known failure  F[Auto fix / auto promotion]
  F   V
  L  unknown or retries exhausted  C[Circuit breaker: stop and alert]
 

  Components
  Component   Purpose   Tech   Owner  
                 
  Orchestrator   Chains promotion and verification per component   TODO   Northwind  
  Dependency promotion   Promotes dependencies from the SBOM   TODO   Northwind  
  Verification build   Runs LTS build per component   TODO   Northwind  
  Failure remediation   Parses logs, classifies failures, applies known fixes   TODO   Northwind  
  Circuit breaker   Stops safely when retries pass a threshold   TODO   Northwind  
  Dashboards   Visibility of runs and results   TODO   Northwind  

  Integrations
TODO: CI and source control, artifact repository.

  Key design decisions
  Decision   Why   Date   Approved by  
                 
  Fully deterministic, no AI/ML   Predictable, traceable releases   2026 04   Charter v1.0  
  Design decisions reviewed by Acme SMEs before build   Client alignment   2026 04   Vantage LTS governance  

  Constraints
Out of scope: artifact repository administration, microservice code changes beyond pipeline compatibility, replacing existing tooling.

  Source documents
  Ion Charter: scope, phases, milestones, success targets.
  Everest Design: architecture and design decisions.

  Showcase
A healthcare technology company released long term versions of its software platform by hand. Each of 27 components needed repeated fix and retry cycles, and one release took two to three months.

Northwind built an automated, deterministic release pipeline. It promotes dependencies from a software bill of materials, runs a verification build per component, classifies failures from the build logs, fixes known failure types automatically and stops safely when retries run out. There is no AI/ML, by design, so every release is predictable and traceable.

Targets: 90% less manual dependency resolution, 80% of failures fixed automatically, 85% or more accuracy in artifact resolution, and the client's own team running the pipeline after handover. A 12 week, fixed scope engagement.

  Ways of working

  Cadence
   Daily:  internal standup (Teams) and an end of day email with three points: done, at risk or blocked, action needed.
   Same day blocker alert:  sent to the blocker owner with description, impact, action, deadline. Escalates after 24 hours unresolved.
   Weekly:  engineering review with Acme Health team; Friday four quadrant status report (accomplishments, in progress, risks and issues, next week).
   Per milestone:  summary email to stakeholders.

  Escalation
  Technical: program manager or engineering team, then Acme Health SMEs, then Acme Health Director.
  Commercial or scope: program manager, then Northwind, then formal Change Request.

  Rule of thumb
Design decisions go to Acme Health SMEs for alignment before implementation starts.

quartz-programme.title: Quartz Programme
quartz-programme.body_text:
Summary
Automate the functional verification of the CARESCAPE Central Station (Meridian) so that regulated, evidence backed six month cyber releases no longer depend on slow, manual testing.

  Details

 Client area:  Acme Health, HC PCS MS Technology
 Our firm:  Northwind
 Status:  the solution design (v1.1, 21 July 2026) is awaiting formal sign off before full scale development.

  Why it exists
Meridian functional verification is manual, repetitive and error prone: 329 verification procedures with 2,711 steps across 6 SVP and 1 DVP documents, with results compared and screenshots captured by hand. Because the Meridian is a regulated medical device, gaps in the evidence can invalidate a run.

  Approach in plain words
  Robot Framework and Python libraries drive the application and produce the evidence.
  Dual driver approach: WinAppDriver and the Java Access Bridge (accessibility tree) for the MFC and Java parts of the UI; computer vision (OpenCV, Tesseract OCR, a trained YOLO model) for complex UI checks.
  Black box: attaches to the running application, no source code or changes to the device.
  Each run produces one consolidated HTML report and a regulatory format PDF with timestamped screenshots.

  Delivery plan (proposal v2)
Hybrid strategy: about 70% manual and 30% selective automation, 24 weeks, fixed scope and milestone based.

  Phase   Focus  
         
  1 Discovery and requirements sign off   Requirements, architecture, environment planning  
  2 Platform foundation   Drivers and vision AI  
  3 Test suite authoring   Test suites in Robot Framework, per component  
  4 Code quality and stabilisation   Review, refactor, self healing, final regression  
  5 Sign off, knowledge transfer and go live   UAT, handover, 90 day hypercare  

  Success targets (proposal v2)
  Driver coverage of 95% or more of identified UI elements
  YOLO detection precision 95% or more, recall 90% or more
  Automated suite 98% or more stable over three consecutive runs
  100% of in scope scenarios traceable from requirement to result
  End state: Acme Health team runs the suite independently

  Open points
  The proposal and the solution design count scope differently (about 2,500 to 3,000 scenarios versus 329 procedures). TODO: confirm the agreed scope.
  Solution design approvers: Emerson Marsh (executive), Remy Finch (technical), Udayashankar Jinde (program), B.S Ganesha (architecture). All pending.

  Showcase
A medical technology company verified a regulated medical device application by hand: 329 verification procedures with 2,711 steps, results compared and screenshots captured manually. Gaps in the evidence could invalidate a whole run.

Northwind is automating the verification with Robot Framework and Python. The suite drives the application as a black box, with no access to its source code, through the Windows UI automation and Java accessibility layers, and uses computer vision (OpenCV, OCR and a trained YOLO model) for complex screens. Each run produces one consolidated HTML report and a regulatory format PDF with timestamped screenshots.

Targets: 95% or more coverage of the user interface, a suite that is 98% or more stable over three consecutive runs, full traceability from requirement to result, and the client's own team running the suite independently.

  Source documents
  Relay Design
  Orbit Proposal (contains commercial terms; internal only)

Summary
Northwind proposal (version 2) to automate the functional verification of the CARESCAPE Central Station. It was won and led to Quartz Programme.

  Details
   Commercial terms:  the document contains them, so it stays internal. Do not share it with the client view or prospects.
   Strategy:  hybrid, about 70% manual and 30% selective automation; 24 weeks, fixed scope and milestone based, in 5 phases, with 90 day hypercare.
   Scope:  about 2,500 to 3,000 scenarios. The solution design counts 329 procedures instead. TODO: confirm the agreed scope.
   Result:  won; the work runs as Quartz Programme.
